turns.learner: Hi! Can we learn comparatives (-er, more ... than) today?
turns.tutor:
Yes! Do you remember how to compare two things in English?

Example: "This shop is cheap. That shop is cheaper than this shop."
Rule: for a short adjective, add -er, then use than to compare two things.
Right: "My bag is smaller than your bag."
Wrong: "My bag is more small than your bag."

Now you try. Write the missing word:
"My street is ___ (long) than your street."
